extracted.intended_audience: early-career AI researchers and research institutions interested in DFG Emmy Noether Programme funding (Germany)
extracted.subtask_description: Information and implicit selection/eligibility criteria for DFG's Emmy Noether Programme call on 'Methods in Artificial Intelligence', describing aims, selection process, eligibility, and strategic priorities. Useful for applicants preparing proposals or institutions hosting groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim: expand methodological and algorithmic foundations of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: All funded projects aim to significantly expand the methodological and algorithmic foundations of artificial intelligence and generate fresh insights into key properties such as robustness, explainability, efficiency and scalability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should target foundational advances in AI methods and provide new insights on properties explicitly named (robustness, explainability, efficiency, scalability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project scope: foundations and domain-specific application potential
rubrics_metrics.description: The projects cover both the mathematical and computer science foundations of neural networks, deep learning and generative AI, as well as domain-specific application potential, addressing such aspects as the harmonisation of heterogeneous geodata, political bias in commercial AI chatbots, and medical risk assessment based on patient data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals may be theoretical/methodological or oriented toward domain applications, but should clearly address either foundational issues or concrete application problems (examples given include geodata harmonisation, political bias, medical risk assessment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process: two-stage proposal submission and international peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The funded projects were selected by means of a two-stage proposal submission and review process. From a total of 178 draft proposals, an internationally recognised panel of experts selected 36, whose applicants were then invited to submit proposals. 15 of these were selected for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should expect an initial draft-stage screening followed by invitation to submit full proposals; evaluation is by an internationally recognised expert panel. High competition (e.g., 178 drafts → 36 invitations → 15 awards) suggests emphasis on excellence and selectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: target group (career stage and employment status)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Emmy Noether Programme is aimed at highly qualified postdoctoral researchers and junior professors with temporary contracts in the early stages of their academic careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be in early career phases (postdocs or junior professors) holding temporary contracts; the scheme is intended to support transition to independent professorship-level leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent group leadership and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: It enables them to qualify for a university professorship by independently leading an Emmy Noether Group over a period of six years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must propose an independent research group whose leadership over six years is central to the qualification objective; plan should demonstrate capacity for independent management and progression toward a professorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and retention objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The group of funding recipients is diverse in terms of background, geographical location, gender and career stage, with researchers in early career phases benefiting in particular. The aim is to counter the brain drain by offering attractive research conditions in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DFG values diversity (background, geography, gender, career stage) and projects that contribute to attracting/retaining researchers to Germany; proposals and host institutions that demonstrate contribution to these objectives may be favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with DFG strategic funding initiative in AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding for Emmy Noether Groups focusing on artificial intelligence methods is one of two priorities within the DFG’s strategic funding initiative in the field of artificial intelligence, adopted in 2019 and updated in 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should align with the DFG's declared strategic priorities in AI methods; familiarity with the initiative (and its 2024 update) and how the project advances that strategy is relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scale and call timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The initiative enables up to 45 Emmy Noether Groups to be funded across four rounds of calls. The fourth and, for the time being, final call was issued on 1 April 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should note the overall program envelope (up to 45 groups across rounds) and that this specific call is the fourth round; timing and remaining opportunities may be limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possibility of special/connected funding (Global Minds Initiative Germany - GMIG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Four of these awards are being made in connection with the DFG’s participation in the Global Minds Initiative Germany. GMIG indicates funding in connection with the DFG’s participation in the Global Minds Initiative Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some awards may be tied to or co-funded by GMIG; applicants should be aware of linked funding streams and any associated expectations or eligibility nuances for GMIG-supported awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attracting researchers from abroad / host-location considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The funding will enable researchers who were previously active in France, the United Kingdom, Sweden and the Netherlands to establish independent AI research groups in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A demonstrated ability to attract international researchers (including those returning from other countries) and to establish groups at German host institutions is consistent with program goals; host institutions should be prepared to offer attractive conditions.
